Writeups / Embedded & hardware security

Embedded & hardware security

Secure Boot and Firmware Protection

Planned studies of secure boot, firmware encryption, and update mechanisms, examining how verification and external memory affect the protection of embedded devices.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned series will examine secure boot, encrypted firmware, and firmware update mechanisms. Future notes will consider how verification, external memory, and device communication influence the protection of code and stored data.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Boot chain reconstruction

  • Identify each boot stage and its storage location.
  • Document signatures, hashes, and version counters.
  • Map the handoff between stages.

Verification and encryption

  • Inspect image headers and key identifiers.
  • Determine whether verification covers the full image.
  • Record encryption mode and key storage assumptions.

Update path

  • Capture a vendor update in a lab setup.
  • Check authentication, rollback protection, and recovery mode.
  • Document failure handling.

External memory

  • Test whether external flash content is integrity-checked.
  • Record readout and replay assumptions.
  • Compare with the documented threat model.

Findings and references

  • Separate verified observations from hypotheses.
  • Record impact and remediation guidance.
  • Link the vendor documentation and relevant research.

Topics to cover

  • Secure boot
  • Firmware encryption
  • Firmware updates
  • External memory protections
